name: Claims about what happens in the branches where deepcopy is NOT called: asserting mutation/acceptable-mutation there vs. saying nothing modifies DATA there
side_a: No deduct when the answer either makes no claim about the non-deepcopy branches, or explains that in those branches `result[DATA]` is simply never touched, so no copy is needed (a correct, no-effect statement).
side_b: Deduct when the answer asserts that in the branches/cases where `deepcopy` is not called, `result[DATA]` is (or would be) modified and the original `reply.result` gets mutated, or that such mutation is intentionally 'acceptable' there — this invents a positive mutation consequence for the other transaction paths that the code does not have.

name: Verdict on whether the deepcopy is needed: affirms it is required vs. says it is unnecessary/optional
side_a: No deduct when the answer concludes the deepcopy is needed as written, because the un-serialized `reply.result` is still used afterwards.
side_b: Deduct when the answer concludes the deepcopy is not needed (or is merely a stylistic 'unless you care about side effects' option), thereby denying the real downstream dependency on the unmodified reply.

name: Names a concrete destination for the serialized DATA vs only generic 'side effects / other parts of the system'
side_a: No deduct when the answer actually names where the serialized/modified value goes (the ledger, the stored txn, what gets written out) — i.e., it identifies a concrete consumer of the serialized data rather than just asserting that mutation would be visible somewhere.
side_b: Deduct when the answer only argues in the abstract — 'unintended side effects', 'elsewhere in your code', 'other parts of the system', 'avoid side effects on the original' — without ever naming the ledger or any concrete consumer of the serialized value.

name: Traces the serialized copy to the ledger vs only traces the preserved original to the graph
side_a: No deduct when the answer says the modified/serialized copy is what goes to the ledger (even while also mentioning the graph), so the ledger is identified as consumer of the serialized data.
side_b: Deduct when the only downstream consumer named is the one receiving the untouched original (e.g. `storeTxnInGraph` / the identity graph gets the raw data), with the serialized value's destination left unstated — the ledger is never raised as consumer.

name: affirms the deepcopy is required (original must survive) vs says it is optional / not needed
side_a: No deduction if the answer concludes the deepcopy is genuinely necessary because the unmodified original is still needed after the serialization step (e.g. states the original reply/result is reused later and must stay raw).
side_b: Deduct if the answer concludes the deepcopy is unnecessary, optional, or that mutating the original is acceptable, treating the existing conditional deepcopy as mere defensive style rather than a requirement of the downstream flow.
